No entity, observable event, metric or series; 'the immediate future' is not a deadline. The examples named include the author's own organizations (Fermata, Acacia Clinics, Videra Health).

Trait claim that human terror 'will be baked into' artificial intelligence. Outside the five areas; no observable event or benchmark. First row for the passage captured again at owen-0781.
Same passage as owen-0780 ('Computers don't get terrified right now... They're going to learn from us') captured twice in the same post; owen-0780 stands.
Ironic inversion of AI-treaty talk: 'some treaty or plan' to deal with human intelligence. Not one of the five areas; 'going to need' is also normative and names no body or instrument.

AGI arrival ('It's going to happen', 'a matter of time', cannot be stopped) is outside the five areas. No benchmark for 'artificial general intelligence' and no date; 'a matter of time' is not a deadline.
General claim about human behavior ('humans will act crazy'). Not one of the five areas; no observable event. The AGI clause asserts nothing.

'A counter-revolution is brewing' is a slogan: no treatment set, metric, series, threshold or date for a shift toward interventional psychiatry. The drug-efficacy clause is a present-tense judgment, not a forecast.

Promotional claim about the author's own book project (it 'will inform and educate' and lead some readers to durable remission). Own product; 'some readers' and 'durable remission' also have no countable set or observable measure.

Restated call that the ADA 'will be brought to bear in the fight for accessible mental health care'. No actor (DOJ, court, plaintiff), instrument (suit, settlement, ruling) or threshold is named, so no event can be written without invention. 'GAME ON' is a slogan.

Legal inference ('it follows that', 'might follow other psychiatric disabilities') from the DOJ alcohol-use-disorder settlement. No deciding body, observable action or threshold is named for accommodations extending to other psychiatric disabilities or to payer 'fail first' policies. Secondary reading: NOT_FORECAST (present-tense legal reasoning).
Truism about workforce attrition ('You can expect people to leave'). Health-workforce exits are not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice-adoption outcome; no series or threshold.

Claim that lost clinical expertise 'doesn't get replaced in a decade'. Health-workforce claim outside the five areas; no metric or series to resolve 'replaced'. 'In a decade' would otherwise anchor to the statement date plus ten years.
Trend claim that more clinicians 'will run for the exits' as the system pushes harder. Health-workforce attrition is outside the five areas; no series, threshold or date.
'We will all survive without private equity investors' is rhetorical contrast: no company action, market outcome or threshold is asserted, and no exit of private equity from health care is claimed.

Conditional hyperbole ('if we let all the doctors and nurses quit', 'very few of us will survive'). The condition has no countable set and the outcome no series or threshold; population mortality is also outside the five areas.

'The beginning of a remarkable change in the treatment of psychiatric disorders' is a slogan; no treatment set, metric, series or threshold. The NTAP decision it celebrates is already public at the statement date. The author is a SAINT provider (Fermata).

First half of the compound claim: 'every breakthrough treatment' gets 'additional payment models in the future'. 'Every' is a quantifier without a countable set, 'breakthrough treatment' and 'additional payment models' are undefined, and 'opens the door' asserts no decision. The second half is coded at owen-0796-b.

event.asset: Psychedelic medicine (a psychedelic-class drug, or a therapy that administers one) under the Medicare inpatient prospective payment system
event.title: Medicare grants a new technology add-on payment (NTAP) for a psychedelic medicine
event.proposition: CMS approves a Medicare new technology add-on payment (NTAP) for a psychedelic medicine (a psychedelic-class drug, or a therapy that administers one) in an inpatient prospective payment system final rule.
event.criterion: TRUE on the effective date (1 October of the fiscal year) of the Medicare inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS) final rule, published in the Federal Register, that approves a new technology add-on payment for a psychedelic-class drug (psilocybin, MDMA, LSD, DMT or a related compound) or for a therapy that administers one. An NTAP application, a proposed rule, a CPT code, an FDA approval, a Medicaid or commercial payer decision, or a payment for ketamine or esketamine does not count. Resolution source: Federal Register, Medicare IPPS final rule, new technology add-on payment section.

resolution_source.name: Federal Register, Medicare IPPS final rule (new technology add-on payment approvals)

readings: 'this' = the Medicare new technology add-on payment (NTAP) mechanism that the post describes for SAINT; the event is written on that mechanism, not on any payment model in general.
'psychedelic medicine' = a psychedelic-class drug (psilocybin, MDMA, LSD, DMT and related compounds) or a therapy that administers one; ketamine and esketamine are not counted.
'paid for' = approval of the add-on payment in a final rule; an application or a proposed rule is not payment.

records.stage_note: At the statement date no psychedelic-class drug had FDA approval, which an NTAP application requires; the post reports the first NTAP for a neuromodulation treatment (SAINT). No class in base-rates.json covers a Medicare add-on payment decision, so b is null.
records.note: Second half of the compound claim: 'To be very clear, this is how psychedelic medicine will be paid for.' 'This' is read as the Medicare NTAP mechanism the post describes for SAINT, so the event is a CMS NTAP approval for a psychedelic-class drug or therapy. 'Will' sets bin A; asserts true. The claim sentence has no time words and 'in the future' in the preceding sentence is not a deadline, so the item is undated (24-month window). CMS decides; the forecaster holds no disclosed role in CMS and none of his affiliations (Fermata, Acacia Clinics, Ampa and others) is named in the event, so affiliated is false. A coder who reads 'this' as any add-on payment model would write a broader event; the reading is logged.
'More are coming' is a quantifier without a countable set (which coverage advances, which payer, which treatments); 'coming' is not a deadline. The first clause is a call to action.
Promotion of the author's own conference (RAMHT 2024) as 'the hot party'. Own event; also a slogan with no benchmark.
Promise of more podcast conversations on the author's own newsletter. Own organization decides.
Attendance claim for the author's own event (RAMHT 2024, 7 January 2024): Grady Hannah and other innovators 'will be there'. Own event; the organizer sets the speaker list.

Counterfactual causal claim ('if you wanted to prevent schizophrenia... That would prevent a lot of schizophrenia') with the author doubting the condition ('Good luck with that'). No future state is asserted; 'a lot' also has no threshold or series.

Section heading in a post the author frames as satire (a riff on George Santos's Bluesky arrival post). Marked satire; the underlying trend claim (denial of objective reality persists) is also outside the five areas and has no observable event.
